title: Metering Telemetry Gatekeeper: validation + enrichment layer for token accounting streams
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a standalone Gatekeeper service that sits between ingestion hooks and the token-accounting ledger. Responsibilities: strict schema validation, enrichment (tenant mapping, plan multipliers, route->model normalization), provenance stamping, idempotency checks, and short-term buffering for late-arriving attributes. Goal is to reduce downstream reconciliation runs, improve attribution accuracy, and make audit trails deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper deployed in staging behind feature flag and able to proxy production ingestion traffic for one route
All incoming events validated against canonical schema; mismatches logged to a dead-letter stream with example counts
Enrichment completed for tenant_id, plan_id, route_alias, model_variant with <50ms median added latency
Idempotency key lookup prevents duplicate writes for events with identical (session_id, seq, source_ts) tuples
Backfill tooling can reprocess a day of raw events through Gatekeeper and produce bit-identical ledger rows compared to manual reconciliation after mapping changes
notes: Motivation: recent INC-2025-02 showed 3% billing drift caused by late-arrival route metadata and model aliasing. Current reconciliation jobs are expensive and slow. We need a lightweight pre-processing layer to shift correctness left and simplify billing attribution jobs.
design_decisions: Keep Gatekeeper as a separate single-responsibility service (not a library) to allow independent scaling and retries
Use Avro schema registry for canonical event contract to support schema evolution with compatibility checks
Use RocksDB local cache for idempotency/windowing with periodic snapshotting to Redis for cross-instance lookups
Perform enrichment synchronously for fast-path attributes; push non-critical enrichments (pricing suggestions) to an async enrichment topic
Expose metrics for validation failure rate, enrichment latency histogram, and ddp (dedup) hit rate for rollout evaluation
tradeoffs: Synchronous enrichment increases tail latency vs doing everything async — mitigated by keeping critical attributes local-cached and setting strict timeout budgets
Maintaining a separate service increases operational surface area but prevents widespread client churn and allows independent rollout cadence
Using RocksDB + Redis adds complexity for recovery; chosen for read-heavy idempotency and low-latency lookups compared to purely Redis approach
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype Gatekeeper binary with validation + enrichment in a sidecar mode for canary route
2) Add Avro schema and CI contract tests (conftest + schema-registry mocking), PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/14689
3) Integrate local RocksDB idempotency store and Redis cross-check; instrument metrics and traces
4) Deploy to staging behind feature flag; run shadow traffic for 72 hours and compare ledger diffs
5) Run controlled backfill for 2025-02-14..2025-02-16 window; surface mismatch report and iterate mapping rules
6) Gradual rollout to production routes with canary percentage and auto-rollback on mismatch threshold
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike complete — validated Avro vs current protobuf payloads; discovered missing route_alias in 0.7% of events. Filed PM mapping task.
2025-02-18: Prototype sidecar running on staging for /v1/generate; median added latency 22ms, p95 90ms. Latency budget acceptable for non-lowest-latency tiers.
2025-02-22: Implemented idempotency local cache (RocksDB) and integrated Redis fallback. Initial stress run shows dedup hit rate ~0.4% under replay tests.

2025-02-27: Backfill harness ready. Running a small backfill for Feb 10-11. First pass shows 0.9% mapping divergence caused by historical plan name changes — PM to provide canonical mapping table (PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Plan+Mapping+Spec).

2025-03-04: Gatekeeper service image pushed to internal registry; staging canary configured (10% shadow traffic). Added Grafana dashboard panel for validation-failure-rate and dead-letter topic size. Next: review by billing team and run two-week shadow run.
